analysis.title: NextDecade Corp. (NEXT): 3Q26 Recap: Progress Towards T1 First LNG; T6+ Growth Requires Commercial Acceleration
key_insights: Management narrowed Rio Grande Train 1 first LNG guidance to 2Q27 from 1H27, slightly later than GS's March 2027 estimate and its view of investor expectations.

T1 substantial completion guidance of 3Q27 is closer to GS's July 2027 estimate, and about one quarter ahead of Bechtel's guaranteed substantial completion. GS now models mid-July 2027, versus early-July 2027 prior.

Management said the balance of Phase 1 tracks about one quarter ahead of guaranteed substantial completion for each train, with potential to accelerate. GS sees the near-term capacity ramp and early volume potential as well telegraphed.

33% of Phase 1 volumes (2027-1Q29) are pre-sold. Management does not plan to lock in incremental volumes during the T1-5 ramp, to avoid being short cargoes during commissioning. GS calls the pause prudent but notes NEXT cannot lock in elevated gas pricing as peers can.

No new SPAs were announced with 3Q26 results. Management expects enough contracts in the next 2-3 quarters to underpin a T6 FID in 2H27. GS estimates about 5 mtpa of contracts are needed, and there are currently no contracts supporting T6.

Contracting conditions look more constructive than a few months ago, as Middle East supply disruptions have spurred LNG supply-security contracting. GS notes reports that QatarEnergy is seeking incremental US LNG supply after its roughly 4 mtpa of SPAs with Cheniere last week.

T6 permitting: US Army Corps permit received in September, and the FERC final Environmental Impact Statement is expected by June 2027. Funding mix (debt, equity or convertible issuance, JV financing) is still under discussion.
GS sees EPC contract line of sight as a key consideration for T6, given Gulf Coast EPC cost inflation and the need for offtake rates that support project returns.

Management selected the west side of the Rio Grande site for T7 and T8, with permitting and commercializing about 1 year behind T6. GS is cautious on underwriting pre-FID growth because Gulf Coast competition is high and some peers undercut SPA rates.

Each +/- $1/mmbtu change in LNG margins moves net DCF to NEXT by $350-400m during the T1-5 ramp. Current prices plus the 33% pre-sold at $3/mmbtu margins support a blended realized margin of $6/mmbtu, or about $400m of incremental net DCF.

Higher ramp-period DCF could speed paydown of the FinCo facilities and ease T6+ funding needs. GS sees minimal leverage capacity after the T5 build-out, and GS EBITDA sits below consensus through 2030.
GS keeps a $8.50 12-month PT (levered DCF, 10% cost of equity, 2% terminal growth) and a Neutral rating. The stock closed at $7.26 on 29 Oct 2026, implying 17.1% upside.

market_movers.rationale: GS keeps Neutral and the $8.50 PT after 3Q26. It expects positive operational updates but wants tangible commercial and funding progress before underwriting T6+ growth.

sector_views.rationale: Contracting for LNG supply security has improved on Middle East disruptions, but Gulf Coast competition is high, some peers undercut SPA rates, and EPC costs are inflating.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 results: no new SPAs were announced. Guidance for Rio Grande T1 first LNG moved to 2Q27 from 1H27, and substantial completion is guided for 3Q27.

GS estimates, all GSe: 2026E Adj. EBITDA of -$230m (previously -$193m), 2027E $411m (previously $467m), 2028E $1,196m (unchanged). 2027E revenue is $2,046.3m (previously $2,222.6m), and 2028E revenue is $5,955.5m (unchanged).

GS EPS estimates, all GSe: 2026E -$1.00 (previously -$1.89), 2027E -$1.51 (previously -$1.24), 2028E -$0.31 (previously -$0.09). Quarterly GSe EPS: 4Q26E -$0.83, 1Q27E -$0.67, 2Q27E -$0.83. 3Q26 EPS was shown as $0.58.

GS Adj. EBITDA estimates: 2029E $1,665m, 2030E $2,540m, 2031E $3,537m, 2032E $3,374m. GS is below consensus through 2030, with consensus 2030E near $3,537m... see Exhibit 3 for the series: 2030E consensus $762m, 2031E $1,479m, 2032E $1,904m is not confirmed by the text.

GS net debt/EBITDA estimates: 36.3x for 2027E and 16.1x for 2028E in the summary table. Consolidated figures in Exhibit 5 are 16.2x (2028E), 14.3x (2029E), 10.4x (2030E), 7.4x (2031E) and 7.6x (2032E).
risk_factors: Higher debt funding requirements and potential equity funding needs from balance sheet constraints.
Lower than expected gas sourcing margins.
Higher than expected run-rate O&M and corporate SG&A.
Lower than expected distributions from a less transparent, complex equity waterfall.
Later than expected equity ownership flips at Train 4 and 5.
EPC cost inflation on the US Gulf Coast and peers undercutting SPA contract rates.
charts_described: Exhibit 2 plots GSe new vs old Adj. EBITDA for 2026E-2032E, with 2026E at -$230m vs -$193m prior and 2027E at $411m vs $467m prior.
Exhibit 5 plots GSe consolidated net debt/EBITDA falling from 16.2x in 2028E to 7.6x in 2032E.
geopolitical: Ongoing supply disruptions from the conflict in the Middle East have spurred contracting for LNG supply security, per GS's Asia energy tour discussion.
Reports that QatarEnergy is seeking incremental US LNG supply after its roughly 4 mtpa of SPAs with Cheniere last week.

tension_points.bull_case: Management targets a T6 FID in 2H27 and expects enough contracts in 2-3 quarters. Middle East disruptions and QatarEnergy's reported search for US LNG supply support contracting, and higher margins could speed FinCo paydown.
tension_points.bear_case: There are no T6 SPAs today and about 5 mtpa are needed. EPC cost inflation, peers undercutting SPA rates, an undecided funding mix and minimal leverage capacity after T5 limit the path.
tension_points.what_invalidates: No sufficient T6 contracts within the next 2-3 quarters, or no clear line of sight to the EPC contract, would undercut a 2H27 T6 FID.
